source_span: These changes shift us away from our previous disinflation outlook into an "oil risk premium" baseline... we pencil in two additional 25bp rate hikes from the Fed in December and March, bringing the target range for the federal funds rate to 4.25-4.50%
source_chain: Sustained (not de-escalating) Middle East-driven oil supply disruptions therefore MS abandons its 'benign de-escalation' baseline for a 45%-probability 'oil risk premium' baseline (17195) therefore inflation is revised up (core PCE 3.2% '26 / 2.7% '27) and growth/labor softened (2027 GDP 2.3% vs 2.6%, payrolls 50k/mo, unemployment 4.3%) therefore the Fed needs two more 25bp hikes (Dec + March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal (17195, 17196), reinforced by the neutral-rate estimate rising to 3.25% from 3.06% and Warsh calling the hike a removal of 'a dose of accommodation' while policy is 'not yet restrictive' (17196); invalidation: a faster Middle East de-escalation or quicker disinflation than projected cuts this to one hike (December only) or none (17196, lines 255-262).
pulse_chain: 10yr yield's break above 5% was unwound mainly by falling oil, not the Fed (DB, matches 17220) therefore the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4% unanimously and raised its neutral-rate estimate to 3.25% from 3.06%, with Warsh framing it as removing accommodation without reaching restrictive (matches 17196) therefore the mechanism underneath is Morgan Stanley's shift to a 45%-probability oil risk premium baseline, which lifts core PCE to 3.2%/2.7%, cuts 2027 GDP to 2.3%, and softens payrolls to 50k/unemployment 4.3% (matches 17195) therefore banks split on the hike path: MS and SocGen call two more hikes (Dec+March) to 4.25-4.50% terminal, Goldman's house view is the Fed underdelivers against ~4 hikes priced (more likely two), HSBC caps it at two-to-three total since 100bp more would put funds rate 150bp above neutral (all figures match 17196/17223/17232/17189) therefore invalidation is MS's own: faster Middle East de-escalation or quicker disinflation leaves only one more hike, in December, with next Friday's payrolls the key release before then (matches 17196, 17220).
why: Every step, figure, bank attribution, and the invalidation condition trace to exact matches in the cited source notes (oil-risk-premium baseline at 45%, identical inflation/growth/payroll revisions, correctly attributed Dec+March MS/SocGen call vs Goldman's underdeliver view vs HSBC's 150bp-above-neutral ceiling, and MS's own de-escalation/disinflation invalidation), with no reversed step, no misattributed argument, and no invented mechanism.
